newsitem.title: USA: Colonial extends distillate allocation through Dec.
newsitem.headline: Colonial extends distillate allocation through Dec.

text.p: Colonial Pipeline Co said it extended the space allocation on its Houston-to-New York distillate line through the month of December.
"The Line Two allocation has been extended through the (month of December," a Colonial spokeswoman said.
The move, due to continued strong demand from product shippers, follows similar allocations that began in late October and extended through November.

The company also said its gasoline line remains open to distillate shipments since shipper demand on that line has not been as voluminous as on the distillate line. The gasoline line was opened to distillate shipments in early November.
The allocations began after a meeting between U.S. Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary and top U.S. energy executives that resulted in a sudden spike in distillate shipping orders.
That meeting was called amid mounting concern surrounding stocks of distillates -- particularly heating oil, which have been far below a year-ago ahead of winter when demand spikes.
The arterial Colonial, the largest refined oil products pipeline in America, includes 960,000 barrel per day (bpd) distillate line and a 1.2 million bpd gasoline line.

Ten companies make up the Atlanta-based Colonial consortium, including Amoco Corp, Atlantic Richfield Co, Petroleos de Venezuela SA's Citgo Petroleum Co unit, DuPont Co's Conoco Inc unit, Mobil Corp, Phillips Petroleum Co, Texaco Inc, Union Oil, a unit of Unocal Corp, and Marathon Oil Co, a unit of USX-Marathon Group.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
